verdict: OK to lend in Sriperumbudur auto components, but only to tier-1/tier-2 suppliers with EV-agnostic product lines and tight monthly monitoring; avoid single-OEM, engine-part-dependent units.
title: Sriperumbudur Auto & Auto Components: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Sriperumbudur is a component-supply cluster feeding the Chennai OEM belt, so the borrower's cash comes from converting steel, aluminium and plastics into parts on a schedule set by one or two OEMs.** Value sits in the tooling and the OEM approval, not the metal; pricing power is thin because the OEM sets the price and the supplier absorbs commodity swings. The working-capital cycle is the whole game: raw material paid upfront, parts delivered on credit, OEM pays late. **So when a proposal lands, check the receivable days against the OEM's payment record, not the borrower's claim; if receivables exceed the peer gross-current-asset norm of 160-170 days [10], ask for the OEM purchase-order and payment-advice trail.**

## What has changed now
**National auto-component output is running hot: IIP NIC 29 is +25.2% YoY and +19.2% Apr-to-date [D], and bank credit to the sector is growing +27.0% against that output [D].** That credit-output gap of +7.8 pp [D] means money is entering faster than goods are leaving, which is exactly where over-trading hides. **The local counter-signal is real: Tamil Nadu GST is -3.2% Apr-to-date against India +6.1% [D], a 9.3 pp gap, so the state's own tax base is shrinking while the national auto print is strong.** Peer results confirm demand is genuine but margins are squeezed by aluminium [5] and commodity risk [6]; Motherson Sumi Wiring grew revenue 46.7% to Rs 4,054 crore with profit up 35% to Rs 223 crore [4]. **Treat the national print as the tailwind and the state GST as the warning; if a borrower's own GST turnover is falling while it asks for higher limits, ask why the cluster is outgrowing its own tax base.**

## Where the growth is
**Pursue tier-2 moulders, aluminium-lightweighting and braking-component makers, and any supplier already shipping EV-agnostic parts, because the OEM shift to EVs is the live demand driver [1][5].** Eicher's 3.92 lakh sq ft lease at Casagrand Industrial Park, Sriperumbudur [2], signals fresh capacity landing in the cluster, so new supplier relationships will form. **Avoid engine-and-drivetrain-only job workers: rating methodology flags engine-part concentration as the highest obsolescence risk as EVs spread [11].** Also avoid single-OEM units with no second approval.

## How to grow safely
**Structure term loans to the tooling and capex, and keep working capital on a separate cash-credit line sized to the OEM receivable cycle, not to the borrower's sales pitch.** Take monthly: OEM payment advices, GST returns, and a stock-and-debtor statement. **Covenant debt/EBITDA at 2.5-2.75x [10]; if a proposal breaches it on projected numbers, ask for the current-year actuals before sanction.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch receivable days stretching past the peer 160-170 day norm [10], a single OEM crossing half of sales, and GST turnover falling against the state's -3.2% [D].** If any two appear together, freeze enhancement and re-price.

- **Monthly:** OEM payment advices and receivable ageing (monthly) -> if receivable days cross 170 [10], cut limit and ask for OEM confirmation.
- **Monthly:** borrower GST turnover vs Tamil Nadu -3.2% [D] (monthly) -> if borrower falls faster than the state, freeze enhancement.
- **Quarterly:** debt/EBITDA from actuals (quarterly) -> if above 2.75x [10], move to secured-only lending.
- **Quarterly:** OEM concentration (quarterly) -> if one OEM crosses half of sales, ask for a second approval letter.
- **Monthly:** commodity pass-through clauses in OEM contracts (monthly) -> if absent, reprice for aluminium risk [5].
